mesh.label: Communicable Diseases
mesh.scopeNote: An illness caused by an infectious agent or its toxins that occurs through the direct or indirect transmission of the infectious agent or its products from an infected individual or via an animal, vector or the inanimate environment to a susceptible animal or human host.

mesh.label: Epidemiology
mesh.scopeNote: Field concerned with the determination of causes, incidence, and characteristic behavior of disease outbreaks affecting human populations. It includes the interrelationships of host, agent, and environment as related to the distribution and control of disease.

mesh.label: Global Health
mesh.scopeNote: A multi- and interdisciplinary field concerned with improving health and achieving equity in health for all people. It transcends national boundaries, promotes cooperation and collaboration within and beyond health science fields, and combines population-based disease prevention with individually-based patient care.

mesh.label: Neurology
mesh.scopeNote: A medical specialty concerned with the study of the structures, functions, and diseases of the nervous system.

mesh.label: Genomic Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: A medical discipline using genomic information about an individual as part of their clinical care (e.g. for diagnostic or therapeutic decision-making) and the health outcomes and policy implications of that clinical use. (From www.genome.gov/health/Genomics-and-Medicine accessed 12/28/2020)

mesh.label: Psychiatry
mesh.scopeNote: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders.

mesh.label: Cardiology
mesh.scopeNote: The study of the heart, its physiology, and its functions.

mesh.label: Medical Informatics
mesh.scopeNote: The field of information science concerned with the analysis and dissemination of medical data through the application of computers to various aspects of health care and medicine.

mesh.label: Medical Oncology
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of neoplasms.

mesh.label: Radiology
mesh.scopeNote: A specialty concerned with the use of x-ray and other forms of radiant energy in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.

mesh.label: Pediatrics
mesh.scopeNote: A medical specialty concerned with maintaining health and providing medical care to children from birth to adolescence.

mesh.label: Quality Improvement
mesh.scopeNote: The attainment or process of attaining a new level of performance or quality.

mesh.label: Endocrinology
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the metabolism, physiology, and disorders of the ENDOCRINE SYSTEM.

mesh.label: Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: A medical specialty concerned with the use of physical agents, mechanical apparatus, and manipulation in rehabilitating physically diseased or injured patients.

mesh.label: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
mesh.scopeNote: An acquired defect of cellular immunity associated with infection by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), a CD4-positive T-lymphocyte count under 200 cells/microliter or less than 14% of total lymphocytes, and increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections and malignant neoplasms. Clinical manifestations also include emaciation (wasting) and dementia. These elements reflect criteria for AIDS as defined by the CDC in 1993.

mesh.label: Health Policy
mesh.scopeNote: Decisions, usually developed by government policymakers, for determining present and future objectives pertaining to the health care system.

mesh.label: Gynecology
mesh.scopeNote: A medical-surgical specialty concerned with the physiology and disorders primarily of the female genital tract, as well as female endocrinology and reproductive physiology.

mesh.label: Pulmonary Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM. It is especially concerned with diagnosis and treatment of diseases and defects of the lungs and bronchial tree.

mesh.label: Gastroenterology
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of the physiology and diseases of the digestive system and related structures (esophagus, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas).

medrxiv.category: intensive care and critical care medicine
medrxiv.name: Critical Care

mesh.label: Critical Care
mesh.scopeNote: Health care provided to a critically ill patient during a medical emergency or crisis.

mesh.label: Nutritional Sciences
mesh.scopeNote: The study of NUTRITION PROCESSES as well as the components of food, their actions, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease.

mesh.label: Ophthalmology
mesh.scopeNote: A surgical specialty concerned with the structure and function of the eye and the medical and surgical treatment of its defects and diseases.

mesh.label: Economics, Medical
mesh.scopeNote: Economic aspects of the field of medicine, the medical profession, and health care. It includes the economic and financial impact of disease in general on the patient, the physician, society, or government.

mesh.label: Occupational Health
mesh.scopeNote: The promotion and maintenance of physical and mental health in the work environment.

mesh.label: Allergy and Immunology
mesh.scopeNote: A medical specialty concerned with the hypersensitivity of the individual to foreign substances and protection from the resultant infection or disorder.

mesh.label: Reproductive Health
mesh.scopeNote: The state of the REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM when functioning optimally without evidence of disease, disorders, or deficiencies.

mesh.label: Geriatrics
mesh.scopeNote: The branch of medicine concerned with the physiological and pathological aspects of the aged, including the clinical problems of senescence and senility.

mesh.label: General Surgery
mesh.scopeNote: A specialty in which manual or operative procedures are used in the treatment of disease, injuries, or deformities.

mesh.label: Primary Health Care
mesh.scopeNote: Care which provides integrated, accessible health care services by clinicians who are accountable for addressing a large majority of personal health care needs, developing a sustained partnership with patients, and practicing in the context of family and community. (JAMA 1995;273(3):192)

mesh.label: Nephrology
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the kidney.

mesh.label: Pharmacology, Clinical
mesh.scopeNote: The branch of pharmacology that deals directly with the effectiveness and safety of drugs in humans.

mesh.label: Education, Medical
mesh.scopeNote: Use for general articles concerning medical education.

mesh.label: Pathology
mesh.scopeNote: A specialty concerned with the nature and cause of disease as expressed by changes in cellular or tissue structure and function caused by the disease process.

mesh.label: Emergency Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: The branch of medicine concerned with the evaluation and initial treatment of urgent and emergent medical problems, such as those caused by accidents, trauma, sudden illness, poisoning, or disasters. Emergency medical care can be provided at the hospital or at sites outside the medical facility.

mesh.label: Rheumatology
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of inflammatory or degenerative processes and metabolic derangement of connective tissue structures which pertain to a variety of musculoskeletal disorders, such as arthritis.

mesh.label: Hematology
mesh.scopeNote: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with morphology, physiology, and pathology of the blood and blood-forming tissues.

mesh.label: Behavior, Addictive
mesh.scopeNote: The observable, measurable, and often pathological activity of an organism that portrays its inability to overcome a habit resulting in an insatiable craving for a substance or for performing certain acts. The addictive behavior includes the emotional and physical overdependence on the object of habit in increasing amount or frequency.

mesh.label: Sports Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: The field of medicine concerned with physical fitness and the diagnosis and treatment of injuries sustained in exercise and sports activities.

mesh.label: Dentistry
mesh.scopeNote: The profession concerned with the teeth, oral cavity, and associated structures, and the diagnosis and treatment of their diseases including prevention and the restoration of defective and missing tissue.

mesh.label: Pain Management
mesh.scopeNote: A form of therapy that employs a coordinated and interdisciplinary approach for easing the suffering and improving the quality of life of those experiencing pain.

mesh.label: Dermatology
mesh.scopeNote: A medical specialty concerned with the skin, its structure, functions, diseases, and treatment.

mesh.label: Otolaryngology
mesh.scopeNote: A surgical specialty concerned with the study and treatment of disorders of the ear, nose, and throat.

mesh.label: Orthopedics
mesh.scopeNote: A specialty which utilizes medical, surgical, and physical methods to treat and correct deformities, diseases, and injuries to the skeletal system, its articulations, and associated structures.

mesh.label: Nursing
mesh.scopeNote: The field of nursing care concerned with the promotion, maintenance, and restoration of health.

mesh.label: Anesthesia
mesh.scopeNote: A state characterized by loss of feeling or sensation. This depression of nerve function is usually the result of pharmacologic action and is induced to allow performance of surgery or other painful procedures.

mesh.label: Transplantation
mesh.scopeNote: Transference of a tissue or organ from either an alive or deceased donor, within an individual, between individuals of the same species, or between individuals of different species.

mesh.label: Urology
mesh.scopeNote: A surgical specialty concerned with the study, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases of the urinary tract in both sexes, and the genital tract in the male. Common urological problems include urinary obstruction, URINARY INCONTINENCE, infections, and UROGENITAL NEOPLASMS.

mesh.label: Ethics, Medical
mesh.scopeNote: The principles of professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the physician, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the physician in patient care and interpersonal relations with patient families.

mesh.label: Palliative Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: A branch of medicine concerned with preventing and relieving the suffering of patients in any stage of disease. Its focus is on comprehensive care and improving the quality of all areas of the patient's life.

mesh.label: Toxicology
mesh.scopeNote: The science concerned with the detection, chemical composition, and biological action of toxic substances or poisons and the treatment and prevention of toxic manifestations.

mesh.label: Forensic Medicine
mesh.scopeNote: The application of medical knowledge to questions of law.

mesh.label: Neurosciences
mesh.scopeNote: The scientific disciplines concerned with the embryology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, etc., of the nervous system.

mesh.label: Microbiology
mesh.scopeNote: The study of microorganisms such as fungi, bacteria, algae, archaea, and viruses.

mesh.label: Computational Biology
mesh.scopeNote: A field of biology concerned with the development of techniques for the collection and manipulation of biological data, and the use of such data to make biological discoveries or predictions. This field encompasses all computational methods and theories for solving biological problems including manipulation of models and datasets.

mesh.label: Cell Biology
mesh.scopeNote: The study of the structure, behavior, growth, reproduction, and pathology of cells; and the function and chemistry of cellular components.

mesh.label: Genomics
mesh.scopeNote: The systematic study of the complete DNA sequences (GENOME) of organisms. Included is construction of complete genetic, physical, and transcript maps, and the analysis of this structural genomic information on a global scale such as in GENOME WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES.

mesh.label: Biological Evolution
mesh.scopeNote: The process of cumulative change over successive generations through which organisms acquire their distinguishing morphological and physiological characteristics.

mesh.label: Biophysics
mesh.scopeNote: The study of PHYSICAL PHENOMENA and PHYSICAL PROCESSES as applied to living things.

mesh.label: Ecology
mesh.scopeNote: The branch of science concerned with the interrelationship of organisms and their ENVIRONMENT, especially as manifested by natural cycles and rhythms, community development and structure, interactions between different kinds of organisms, geographic distributions, and population alterations. (Webster's, 3d ed)

mesh.label: Neoplasms
mesh.scopeNote: New abnormal growth of tissue. Malignant neoplasms show a greater degree of anaplasia and have the properties of invasion and metastasis, compared to benign neoplasms.

mesh.label: Allergy and Immunology
mesh.scopeNote: A medical specialty concerned with the hypersensitivity of the individual to foreign substances and protection from the resultant infection or disorder.

mesh.label: Biochemistry
mesh.scopeNote: The study of the composition, chemical structures, and chemical reactions of living things.

mesh.label: Molecular Biology
mesh.scopeNote: A discipline concerned with studying biological phenomena in terms of the chemical and physical interactions of molecules.

mesh.label: Plant Physiological Phenomena
mesh.scopeNote: The physiological processes, properties, and states characteristic of plants.

mesh.label: Genetics
mesh.scopeNote: The branch of science concerned with the means and consequences of transmission and generation of the components of biological inheritance. (Stedman, 26th ed)

mesh.label: Bioengineering
mesh.scopeNote: The application of engineering principles and methods to living organisms or biological systems.

mesh.label: Developmental Biology
mesh.scopeNote: The field of BIOLOGY which deals with the process of the GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT of an organism.

mesh.label: Systems Biology
mesh.scopeNote: Comprehensive, methodical analysis of complex biological systems by monitoring responses to perturbations of biological processes. Large scale, computerized collection and analysis of the data are used to develop and test models of biological systems.

mesh.label: Physiology
mesh.scopeNote: The biological science concerned with the life-supporting properties, functions, and processes of living organisms or their parts.

mesh.label: Behavior, Animal
mesh.scopeNote: The observable response an animal makes to any situation.

mesh.label: Pharmacology
mesh.scopeNote: The study of the origin, nature, properties, and actions of drugs and their effects on living organisms.

mesh.label: Synthetic Biology
mesh.scopeNote: A field of biological research combining engineering in the formulation, design, and building (synthesis) of novel biological structures, functions, and systems.

mesh.label: Pathology
mesh.scopeNote: A specialty concerned with the nature and cause of disease as expressed by changes in cellular or tissue structure and function caused by the disease process.

mesh.label: Zoology
mesh.scopeNote: The study of animals - their morphology, growth, distribution, classification, and behavior.

mesh.label: Epidemiology
mesh.scopeNote: Field concerned with the determination of causes, incidence, and characteristic behavior of disease outbreaks affecting human populations. It includes the interrelationships of host, agent, and environment as related to the distribution and control of disease.

mesh.label: Communication
mesh.scopeNote: The exchange or transmission of ideas, attitudes, or beliefs between individuals or groups.

mesh.label: Paleontology
mesh.scopeNote: The study of early forms of life through fossil remains.

mesh.label: Clinical Trials as Topic
mesh.scopeNote: Works about pre-planned studies of the safety, efficacy, or optimum dosage schedule (if appropriate) of one or more diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques selected according to predetermined criteria of eligibility and observed for predefined evidence of favorable and unfavorable effects. This concept includes clinical trials conducted both in the U.S. and in other countries.
